newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent trades weaker, U.S. arbitrage widens.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent trades weaker, U.S. arbitrage widens.

text.p: Dated Brent's discount to October paper widened further on Tuesday as length piled up and the U.S. arbitrage stayed shut, dealers said.
However, there were signs that the transatlantic arb may open soon as NYMEX crude rallied more strongly than IPE on Tuesday afternoon.
A Brent loading on Sept 16-18 was sold at Oct -17 cents on Tuesday afternoon, seven cents below Monday, while Oct Brent recovered early losses to stand at $22.60 per barrel, steady on the day.
Oct/Nov Brent slipped five cents to +60 cents.
"There is no arbitrage at the moment, a lot of people are holding cargoes and a lot of people are short paper. I don't think anyone wants Brent to go up," a North Sea equity holder said.
With the backwardation easing and Brent softer, dealers said the recent recovery of Norwegian differentials may have peaked.
They said there were still some September loadings of most grades on offer, and Ekofisk traded at a similar level to last done. An end-month loader was sold at Dated Brent +36 cents.
In the Mediterranean, sentiment stayed firm on a mixture of loading delays in Novorossiisk and strong refiner demand.
Urals was on offer at Dated Brent -75 cents cif Augusta, but buyers were reluctant to commit to the new higher prices.
Bad weather suspended loadings at Novorossiisk over last weekend, exacerbating the existing 5-6 day delay in the September loading schedule.
A cargo of Iranian heavy was expected to be sold into the Mediterranean in September, but Syrian Light was sold out following last week's trades at a premium to the OSP.
